quickAnswer: Needham's median home value is $1,076,900, the 5th-highest of the 50 towns we serve, and its houses run from 1939-or-earlier originals to homes built since 2010. At that value, a heating or cooling system deserves careful sizing, not a guess.
body: ## What a $1,076,900 median home asks of a heating system

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) puts the typical owner-occupied Needham home at $1,076,900, fifth among the 50 towns we serve. Needham is also the 6th-largest of the 50 by population, with 31,957 residents. A house worth that much is a good reason to size the system carefully and to look at the whole house, not just the old unit. Even temperatures from floor to floor depend on the load calculation, the ducts or piping and the controls.
## Old houses and new ones

Needham's housing is unusually split. The median home was built in 1963, and 7,806 homes, 66.7%, predate 1980. The largest band is the 3,229 homes (27.6%) from 1940 to 1959, and another 2,253 (19.2%) are from 1939 or earlier. Wikipedia says the town's population grew by over 50 percent during the 1930s, which fits those early bands. Needham was first settled in 1680 and incorporated in 1711, yet the Census counts show most of today's housing arrived in the twentieth century.

At the same time, 2,396 homes (20.5%) date from 2000 or later, and 1,426 of them (12.2%) from 2010 or later, the 8th-highest share of the 50 towns. Old and new homes need different things. An older house may have radiators, an aging boiler and limited insulation. A newer one can be tight and ducted, with several zones and a large cooling load. They are separate problems.
## Still a third on oil

Utility gas heats 5,942 occupied homes (52.5%), but fuel oil or kerosene still heats 3,644 (32.2%), a little below the 36.5% of the middle town. Electricity heats 1,319 homes (11.7%) and bottled gas 279 (2.5%). For an oil owner, a failed boiler is a real decision point: another oil system, a conversion to gas if a main is available, or a heat pump. With houses at these values, it can help to have all three priced before choosing. Detached houses are 9,056 of the 11,710 units (77.3%), close to the 76.7% of the middle town. Renters hold 1,605 of the 11,312 occupied homes (14.2%), against 16.4% in the middle town.
## The Charles River and the Back Bay fill

Wikipedia notes that the Charles River forms nearly all of the southern and northeastern boundaries of the town, and that elevations range from 85 feet above sea level at Rosemary Meadows to 180 feet at Needham Square and 300 feet at Bird's Hill. The town has a warm-summer humid continental climate with high humidity and precipitation year-round, which matters for basements and for cooling. It covers 12.7 square miles, shaped like a northward-pointing triangle.

In 1857 Boston began filling the Back Bay, and the fill was taken from Needham, from the area of present-day Route 128. Railroad contractors built 6 miles of track for 35-car trains that made 16 trips a day. The town hall on the common was dedicated on December 22, 1903, and refurbished and expanded in 2011. The town was incorporated in 1711.
## Rebates when the utility is not on file

Our records do not name the electric utility for Needham addresses, so we name none here. Whichever utility serves your address is the one that runs the heat pump rebate, and the 2026 figures are set out on the [heat pump page](/cities/needham/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits). Your electric bill shows who supplies your power.

faq.q: Why does a Needham heating project start with an assessment?
faq.a: Because the houses vary a great deal. The median home is worth $1,076,900, and 19.2% date from 1939 or earlier while 12.2% were built in 2010 or later. That spread is why a load assessment comes first, and why the options go into a written estimate before any work starts.

faq.q: A third of Needham homes burn oil. Should I switch?
faq.a: Maybe. Oil heats 32.2% of occupied homes here, and gas heats 52.5%. If a main reaches your street, a conversion is possible, and a heat pump is another route. The right answer depends on your house, your street and your budget, so we price the options together.

faq.q: Do newer Needham homes need less HVAC attention?
faq.a: Not less, but different. About 12.2% of homes were built in 2010 or later. They are usually tight, so ventilation, humidity and zoning matter more than air leaks. Filters, controls and cooling sizing deserve a close look.

faq.q: Who is my electric utility in Needham?
faq.a: Check your electric bill. We have not confirmed the utility for every address, and Mass Save or a municipal program can only apply through the one that serves you. Once you know, the heat pump rebates and their conditions can be checked at masssave.com.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Needham splits between gas and oil, in houses from every era. A replacement starts with a load assessment of the actual house and a decision about fuel, since a main does not reach every street.
body: ## Replacing heat in a town that has both oil and gas

About half of Needham's occupied homes use gas and about a third use oil, with the rest on electricity or bottled gas. That leaves three routes for a replacement: a like-for-like oil swap, a switch to gas and a move to heat pumps. We start by finding out what is already in the basement and what is available on the street.
### Two houses on one street

Older houses, from before 1940 into the postwar years, can have hot-water or steam heat, plaster walls and rooms of very different sizes. Newer houses can be ducted, with several zones and a tight envelope. A boiler for one is a different job from a furnace for the other, and neither should be copied from what was there before.
### What we check

- The heating load, calculated from the house and not the old nameplate.
- The vent path and gas piping, since that is where an inspection looks.
- Radiators, baseboard or ducts, and whether they can handle a different supply temperature.
- Where the unit sits and how the flue gas is exhausted.
### The permit
Putting in a gas appliance sets off a permit and a closing inspection. In Massachusetts the permit has to come from a licensed plumber or gas fitter, so ask who is applying before you sign.

### Small buildings
In the 372 two-family buildings, the heating may be shared or separate, and the first job is finding out which.
### Oil to something else

Moving from oil to gas means a new gas line, a meter and removal or abandonment of the oil tank, which has to be handled properly. Moving to a heat pump may mean new electrical capacity. Each path has costs that only show up when someone walks the house, and we give you a written estimate before work begins.
### Repair or replace

A failed circulator, a bad igniter or a clogged nozzle is a repair. A cracked heat exchanger or a boiler leaking at the sections is not. The cost of the repair relative to the remaining life of the system decides it.
If your heat fails, call (508) 786-8755. Emergency calls are taken 24 hours a day. The [maintenance page](/cities/needham/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers what a yearly visit prevents.

faq.q: Can Needham homeowners get an estimate for several fuel options?
faq.a: Yes. Where it is practical we can price oil, gas and a heat pump for the same house, in writing, before any work starts. Gas is only on the table if a main serves your street.

faq.q: Does a boiler replacement in an older Needham house need new radiators?
faq.a: Usually not. Many radiators can be reused with a new boiler. We check the piping and the venting, and we size the boiler to the load of the house, which is often lower than the old unit.

faq.q: Is another oil boiler a reasonable choice in Needham?
faq.a: It can be. Oil still heats 3,644 Needham homes (32.2%), so it is a normal choice rather than an outdated one. Compare it with gas, if a main reaches your street, and with a heat pump. The written estimate can show all three side by side.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Needham summers are humid, and cooling needs differ between homes built before 1940 and those built since 2010, from ductless heads to zoned ducted systems. Sizing and moisture control come first.
body: ## Cooling the house, not just the thermostat

Per Wikipedia, Needham sits in a warm-summer humid continental climate where humidity and precipitation stay high all year. Drying the air is half of a cooling system's job, and an oversized unit skips it: the thermostat is satisfied quickly and the compressor stops before much moisture has left the house.
### Newer homes, bigger loads

Needham has 1,426 homes dating from 2010 or later. Newer houses can have tall ceilings, large windows and open plans, which raise the cooling load, along with several zones. Getting the zoning and duct design right matters as much as the tonnage. A system with one thermostat for a three-level house can leave some rooms warm.
### Older homes with no ducts

Central air was not yet common when the 3,229 homes from 1940 to 1959, Needham's largest age band, were built. In a radiator-heated house of that era there may be little space for ductwork, and finished plaster ceilings can make new runs expensive. A ductless mini-split sidesteps the problem with one outdoor unit and a small indoor head in each room you want cooled. High-velocity duct systems are another option where an attic or closet can take the lines.
### Condos and attached homes

Some Needham homes are in larger multi-unit buildings, with 1,496 in buildings of five or more units, and 696 are townhouses. Yard space can be tight, and a condominium association may say where equipment sits and how much noise it makes. A written estimate with the equipment details gives the board something to review.

### A median home worth $1,076,900
With the fifth-highest median value of the 50 towns, a cooling system that leaves one floor warm is an expensive miss. That is the argument for spending design time on zoning and duct layout rather than just picking a tonnage.
### Heat pumps cool too

A heat pump is an air conditioner that also runs in reverse. Where a house needs cooling and also has an aging oil boiler, pricing both jobs together can be sensible. See the [heat pump page](/cities/needham/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) for how that works.
### Repair or replace
A bad capacitor or dirty coil is a repair. A dead compressor in an old unit tends to settle the question in favor of replacement. We explain which case you are in and leave the estimate in writing.

faq.q: How do I cool a three-story Needham house evenly?
faq.a: Zoning. One thermostat cannot serve three floors with different sun and heat gain. Separate zones or ductless heads on the top floor are common fixes, and the design starts with a load calculation.

faq.q: Can I add central air to a 1940s Needham house?
faq.a: Often, but it takes work. A compact duct system in the attic or a ductless setup avoids tearing up plaster. We look at attic space and layout before recommending one.

faq.q: Why is my Needham house clammy even with the air conditioning on?
faq.a: Usually the unit is cooling the air without running long enough to dry it. Needham has high humidity and precipitation year-round, so moisture control matters as much as temperature. An oversized unit is a common cause. Sizing from the load of the house, and sometimes adding a dehumidifier, addresses it.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: About a third of Needham homes burn oil (3,644 homes, 32.2%), and 20.5% date from 2000 or later. Both facts shape heat pump decisions here. The rebate runs through whichever utility serves the address, and we have not confirmed Needham's.
body: ## Heat pumps in a town with 3,644 oil homes

Oil heats 3,644 Needham homes (32.2%), a little under the 36.5% of the middle town, while gas heats 5,942 (52.5%) and electricity 1,319 (11.7%). For an oil owner a heat pump is one of three routes, next to another oil boiler and a gas conversion. Gas-heated houses are the other group: a heat pump can cover mild weather and leave the furnace for the coldest days.
### Rebate and utility, briefly

The Mass Save 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton up to $8,500, with weatherization required first, and it flows through the electric utility serving the address, which we have not confirmed for Needham. Every other condition sits on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Age bands against the 2000 cutoff

The newest group is large here: 2,396 homes (20.5%) were built in 2000 or later, and 1,426 of them (12.2%) in 2010 or later, the 8th-highest share of the 50 towns. Those houses clear the age test on their own. The other end is 7,806 homes (66.7%) built before 1980, with 2,253 from 1939 or earlier, and those owners should expect an energy assessment to come first.
### Ducted or ductless
- **Ducted:** reuses good ductwork and suits newer houses with zoning.
- **Ductless:** one head per room or zone, no ducts needed, which suits the radiator-heated houses of the mid-century.
- **A mix:** ducted units on the main levels with a mini-split in an addition suit some houses.
### Housing types

Of the 11,710 housing units, 9,056 are detached houses, 696 are townhouses and 372 sit in two-family buildings. In a two-family house the question is whether one system or two should serve it, and which meter each one uses. Our [cooling page](/cities/needham/air-conditioning-installation-repair) covers the summer side. Ask for the calculation behind any quote, since sizing decides how a heat pump behaves on the coldest days.

faq.q: Which utility serves my Needham address?
faq.a: We have not confirmed Needham's utility, so check your electric bill. Where a municipal utility serves the address, the rebate path is different from where a Mass Save sponsor does, and masssave.com explains how. Knowing the answer before you plan saves a surprise later.

faq.q: Can I keep my oil boiler and add a heat pump?
faq.a: Yes. The heat pump can carry most of the season and the boiler can cover the coldest hours. That is a partial-home setup, and our main heat pump page has the partial-home figures. In a town where 32.2% of homes burn oil, it is a common question.

faq.q: Do heat pumps work in Needham winters?
faq.a: Cold-climate models are designed for them. Installation quality and correct sizing matter more than brand, and a house can keep its oil or gas heat as a backup for the coldest days, so the heat pump does not have to carry everything.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: With oil heating 3,644 Needham homes, annual burner cleaning matters for about a third of the town. Gas, electric and heat pump systems need their own yearly checks, best done before October.
body: ## Maintenance in a town that heats three ways

Needham homes use gas, oil and electricity in real numbers, so a good maintenance plan starts with the fuel. For the oil homes, the annual visit is a cleaning: burner, nozzle, filter, heat exchanger and combustion. For gas homes the visit looks at the burner, venting and controls. For electric and heat pump homes it is coils, filters, drains and refrigerant checks.
### Why oil owners should not skip a year

Soot builds up between cleanings, reducing efficiency and sometimes causing a shutdown in the coldest week. A yearly cleaning beats an emergency call, and it gives the technician a chance to spot a leaking tank line or a failing pump.
### Equipment that has been replaced before

In a house built before 1940, the current equipment may be a replacement for the original, and it may be due for a look. A tune-up on a mid-life system tells you how it is doing and what to expect, which helps if you are planning renovations that will change the load.

### What the numbers say about age
The median Needham home dates to 1963, 66.7% were built before 1980, and 19.2% go back to 1939 or earlier. The 2,396 homes from 2000 on are a different case, so one plan does not fit both.
### Newer homes

- Filters in a tight house get dirty faster, and dirty ones strain the blower.
- Condensate drains on high-efficiency units can clog.
- Zone dampers and controls need an occasional check.
- Humidifier pads and water valves need annual attention.
### Seasonal rhythm

- **Early fall:** heating checks, before the first real cold.
- **Spring:** a look at central air and mini-splits before the first hot week.
- **Any time:** noise, smell or a change in how the house feels.
### What to tell us

Fuel, age of the system, any model number you can read, whether the equipment sits in a basement or an attic, and what you noticed. Our [heating page](/cities/needham/heating-installation-repair) explains what happens if it turns out to need replacement.

faq.q: How often should I service an oil boiler?
faq.a: Every year, before the heating season. About a third of Needham homes burn oil, and the cleaning keeps soot from building up and lets the technician catch worn parts, such as a tired pump or a weeping tank line, before they fail on a cold night.

faq.q: Is maintenance worth it on a new heat pump?
faq.a: Yes. Filters, coils and drains still need attention, and a check confirms the refrigerant side is working properly. Outdoor units also need clearance from leaves and snow, and a visit before the season is the time to confirm both.

faq.q: Do the newest Needham houses need yearly service too?
faq.a: Yes, though the checklist differs. Needham has 1,426 homes built since 2010. Condensate drains, filters, zone controls and humidifier parts are the usual items, and a visit confirms they still work properly before the season starts.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Needham has homes from 1939 or earlier and homes built since 2010. Older houses leak and hold dust and damp, while tight new ones need ventilation and humidity control. The fix depends on the house.
body: ## Two kinds of air problems in one town
About one Needham home in five dates from 1939 or earlier, and about one in eight from 2010 or later. The two groups breathe very differently.

### The middle bands
Age alone does not say how tight a house is. The largest single band in town is the 3,229 homes (27.6%) from 1940 to 1959, and the 1,508 homes from 1980 to 1999 sit between the leaky and the tight. For them an inspection of the actual house tells more than the year on the deed.
### The older house

Homes from the early twentieth century tend to be leaky, with gaps at the sills, windows and attic. That keeps indoor air from getting stale but pulls in dust, pollen and basement air. Old ducts, where they exist, can carry years of dust. Before a renovation disturbs old paint or insulation, have a qualified specialist test it.
### The tight new house

Modern houses are built to leak little. The trade-off is that moisture and cooking fumes stay in the house unless mechanical ventilation moves them out. Bath fans, range hoods and sometimes an ERV or HRV are what make a tight house healthy. Filters need changing on time because the system moves a lot of air.

### Two numbers to remember
The oldest group, the 2,253 homes from 1939 or earlier, is 19.2% of the town. The tightest group, the 1,426 homes from 2010 or later, is 12.2%. Between them lie the rest of the housing stock, where the answer can go either way.
### Humidity

Needham has high humidity and precipitation year-round, according to Wikipedia, and parts of town lie along the Charles River. Basements can be damp and finished basements can hold moisture in carpets and walls. A dehumidifier treats the air, while a leak or poor grading is a building problem to fix where it starts.
### What helps in most houses

- Better filtration, matched to the blower.
- A basement dehumidifier, and a humidifier on the system only if winter air proves too dry.
- Working exhaust fans in bathrooms and kitchens.
- Duct cleaning only when ducts are dirty, moldy or damaged.
### Testing

One reading of humidity, carbon monoxide or particles shows a single moment. Use it to find the cause, then fix the cause. Our [cooling page](/cities/needham/air-conditioning-installation-repair) explains how humidity is handled in summer.

faq.q: Do tight new homes need an air exchanger?
faq.a: Often they benefit from one. A very tight house relies on mechanical ventilation to bring in fresh air, and an ERV or HRV does it while limiting energy loss. We can assess if that fits your home.

faq.q: Should I clean the ducts in my older Needham house?
faq.a: Only when they are dirty, moldy or damaged. We look first and say whether cleaning would make a difference.

faq.q: Does a newer Needham house still need a dehumidifier?
faq.a: Sometimes. Needham has high humidity and precipitation year-round, and a tight house lets moisture build up if ventilation is weak. A hygrometer will show whether the basement or bedrooms run damp before you buy equipment.
